name: Dependency Injection
tagline: Inverting collaborator creation to a Composition Root via explicit constructor injection—making services immutable, testable in milliseconds, and free of global state.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Dependency Injection—from constructor injection and Composition Roots to captive dependencies, circular graphs, and compile-time vs runtime containers.

spark.summary: Dependency Injection (DI) flips object creation inside out: instead of a class instantiating its own collaborators with `new`, an external assembler or IoC container supplies those dependencies through constructors or parameters.
spark.keyTakeaway: Prefer explicit constructor injection over field/setter injection so required dependencies are immutable, compiler-checked, and trivially mockable in unit tests.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Dependency Injection (DI)** separates *object graph construction* from *business behavior*.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Wiring an Immutable Dependency Graph at Startup (Composition Root (main) -> OrderController -> OrderService(repo, clk) -> JdbcOrderRepo / Fake); Singleton vs. Request Scope & Provider<T> Boundary (SINGLETON INIT -> REQUEST SCOPE -> CAPTIVE BUG).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose your DI mechanism based on startup-latency budgets and ecosystem needs. In serverless/Lambda or GraalVM native images, prefer compile-time DI (Micronaut/Dagger/Wire) or explicit `@Import` configurations over broad `@ComponentScan`.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore ThreadLocal memory leaks, SOLID principles, GoF patterns, and contract testing.

learningJourney.title: What is Dependency Injection (DI) & Inversion of Control
learningJourney.explanation:
**Dependency Injection (DI)** separates *object graph construction* from *business behavior*. Instead of a service calling `new PostgresClient()` or pulling from global singletons, an external **Composition Root** (`main()`, Spring `@Configuration`, Google Wire) instantiates concrete implementations and passes them in—ideally via constructor parameters typed to interfaces.

**Constructor injection** guarantees a valid, immutable (`final`/`readonly`) object at creation time and lets unit tests pass fast in-memory fakes without starting a container.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Dependency Injection (DI) & Inversion of Control works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Hardcoded `new` Breaks Testing (and How Scopes Prevent Captive State)
learningJourney.explanation: Hardcoding `new PostgresClient()` forces every unit test to spin up real databases and makes swapping implementations (e.g., Razorpay -> PayU, S3 -> MinIO) invasive. When using DI containers, you must also respect **scope lifetimes**: a `Singleton` capturing a `Request`-scoped auth context in its constructor creates a **captive dependency** that leaks User A's state to User B.

comparison.choice: Use: Services Touching I/O, Clocks, Brokers & Feature Flags
benefits: Enables <2 ms deterministic unit tests (`Clock.fixed`) and zero-touch backend swaps.
costs: Keep constructor params <=5; >5 dependencies signals a Single Responsibility violation.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Pure Value Objects & Domain Entities
benefits: `Money`, `OrderLine`, and `StringUtils` have zero side effects and need no DI.

comparison.choice: Avoid: HFT Hot Paths & Tiny <300-Line Scripts
benefits: Manual `main()` wiring avoids reflection proxy overhead and cold-start latency.
costs: Over ~40–50 wired services, manual factory boilerplate becomes tedious.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to Avoid Captive Dependencies, Circular Graphs & Service Locators
learningJourney.explanation:
1. **Bridge Scopes Safely**: Never inject a `Request` bean into a `Singleton` constructor—inject a `Provider<T>` / `ObjectFactory<T>` or pass request context as a method parameter.
2. **Ban Service Locator**: Never inject `ApplicationContext` or `Container.get()` into business classes—it hides true dependencies.
3. **Break Circular Dependencies**: Extract shared logic into a third service or emit an async domain event (`OrderPlacedEvent`).

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Compile-Time DI vs. Runtime Reflection vs. Manual Wiring
learningJourney.explanation: Choose your DI mechanism based on startup-latency budgets and ecosystem needs.

benefits: Immutable (`final`/`readonly`), null-safe at init, works in tests without a container.
costs: Slightly more verbose than `@Autowired` fields (use primary constructors / Lombok).

benefits: <50 ms startup, zero reflection, catches missing/circular bindings at compile time.
costs: Annotation-processor / codegen step; less dynamic runtime AOP magic.

benefits: Rich lifecycle hooks (`@PostConstruct`), AOP proxies, and ecosystem integrations.
costs: Broad `@ComponentScan` adds 3–8s to Lambda/Cloud Run cold starts.

learningJourney.title: Production Architecture: Scope Lifetimes & Async Context Propagation
learningJourney.explanation: In serverless/Lambda or GraalVM native images, prefer compile-time DI (Micronaut/Dagger/Wire) or explicit `@Import` configurations over broad `@ComponentScan`. Also beware `ThreadLocal` request-scoped proxies when offloading work to `ExecutorService` or `asyncio.create_task`—explicitly copy context across thread boundaries.

knowledgeCheck.question: A `Singleton` `OrderService` injects a `Request`-scoped `UserAuthContext` directly into its constructor. In production, every subsequent user sees the very first user's auth context. What is this bug, and how do you fix it?

options.text: A Captive Dependency; inject a `Provider<UserAuthContext>` (or pass the auth context as a method parameter) instead of direct constructor injection
options.feedback: Correct: a Singleton's constructor runs once at startup, capturing the first Request-scoped instance forever unless bridged via `Provider<T>` or method parameters.

options.text: A Circular Dependency; add `@Lazy` to the constructor
options.feedback: This is a scope-lifetime mismatch (Captive Dependency), not a circular graph.

options.text: Switch from constructor injection to `@Autowired` field injection
options.feedback: Field injection on a Singleton still captures the Request bean once at startup.
